name: The Drakensberg
tagline: A 200-kilometre wall of basalt and sandstone peaks, the Dragon Mountains, with waterfalls, hiking trails, ancient San rock paintings and the highest waterfall in Africa.
highlight: Standing beneath the Amphitheatre, a five-kilometre rock wall towering above the Royal Natal National Park.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed mountain range of dramatic escarpments, with the Amphitheatre and Tugela Falls, Cathedral Peak, Giant's Castle, San rock art, hiking, horse riding and mountain resorts.
metaDescription: A Drakensberg travel guide: the Amphitheatre and Tugela Falls, Cathedral Peak, Giant's Castle, San rock art, hiking, Sani Pass, best time, where to stay and a three-day plan.

image.alt: The Amphitheatre, a huge curving rock wall in the Drakensberg mountains

intro: The Drakensberg, Afrikaans for Dragon Mountains and known to the Zulu as uKhahlamba, the Barrier of Spears, is the highest range in southern Africa. Its great basalt escarpment runs for about 200 km along the border between South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province and Lesotho, rising to more than 3,400 metres, with sandstone foothills, deep valleys, grassy slopes and rivers. It was inscribed by UNESCO in 2000 for its spectacular scenery, biodiversity and its rock art.

The most famous sight is the Amphitheatre, a rock wall about 5 km long and 1,200 metres high in the Royal Natal National Park, with the Tugela Falls plunging in five drops over the edge, the second-highest waterfall in the world at about 948 metres. Elsewhere, Cathedral Peak, Champagne Castle and Giant's Castle offer hiking, and the sandstone shelters hold more than 35,000 paintings by the San people, who lived here for thousands of years.

It is a place for walkers, riders, birdwatchers and those who enjoy mountain air. Small resorts and lodges are scattered through the valleys, and the days are best spent on trails, with a swim in a rock pool at the end. Weather can change fast, with summer thunderstorms and winter snow, and a car is the best way to reach the trailheads.

whyVisit.intro: The Drakensberg is South Africa's finest mountain scenery, with excellent walks for all abilities.

points.title: Dramatic escarpment
points.text: Sheer basalt walls, spires and amphitheatres.

points.title: Tugela Falls
points.text: One of the highest waterfalls in the world, reached by a hike.

points.title: Hiking for everyone
points.text: Easy waterfall walks to multi-day treks.

points.title: San rock art
points.text: Thousands of paintings in shelters, some up to 3,000 years old.

points.title: Mountain resorts
points.text: Family-friendly lodges with horse riding and swimming holes.

attractionsIntro: The range has several distinct areas, each with its own character.

attractions.name: The Amphitheatre and Royal Natal National Park
attractions.text: A great curving rock wall with the Tugela Falls behind. Trails lead to the Tugela Gorge, and a hike to the top via chain ladders from Sentinel car park reaches the escarpment.

attractions.name: Tugela Falls

image.alt: The Tugela Falls dropping from the top of the Amphitheatre

attractions.text: A waterfall in five drops totalling about 948 metres, often cited as the second highest in the world. It flows best after rain, and can freeze in winter.
attractions.tip: Check the flow before you go.

attractions.name: Cathedral Peak

image.alt: The distinctive rock tower of Cathedral Peak in the Drakensberg

attractions.text: A sharp, cathedral-like peak in the central Drakensberg, with hiking trails, rock pools and Didima Gorge, and access to San rock art.

attractions.name: San rock art at Giant's Castle and Cathedral Peak

image.file: File:ELANDS - Eland figures in San rock art at Eland Cave, South Africa, 2017.jpg
image.alt: San rock paintings of eland antelope on the wall of Eland Cave

attractions.text: The Drakensberg holds one of the world's greatest collections of rock art, with paintings of eland, humans and spirit beings, at sites such as Main Caves and Eland Cave.

attractions.name: Giant's Castle Game Reserve
attractions.text: A high-altitude reserve with eland, other antelope and the rare bearded vulture, which can be seen at a hide in winter.

attractions.name: Sani Pass
attractions.text: A 4x4 route over the escarpment into Lesotho, with steep hairpins, and the highest pub in Africa at the top.

thingsToDoIntro: Walking and outdoor activities make up most of the days.

thingsToDo.title: Hike to Tugela Gorge
thingsToDo.text: A 5-hour walk through a spectacular gorge to the base of the Amphitheatre.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a horse
thingsToDo.text: Trails through the foothills and valleys.

thingsToDo.title: Fly fish for trout
thingsToDo.text: Rivers and dams stocked with trout.

foodIntro: Mountain lodges serve hearty meals, with braais and traditional dishes.

accommodation.intro: Stay in a mountain lodge, resort or self-catering cottage in one of the valleys.

areas.name: Champagne Valley and Central Berg
areas.text: Resorts and lodges beneath Champagne Castle.

areas.name: Royal Natal and the Northern Berg

gettingThere.intro: The Drakensberg is 350 to 450 km from Johannesburg and Durban.

options.text: About 4 to 5 hours to the central Berg.

gettingAround.intro: A car is essential for trailheads and valleys.

options.text: Roads are paved to most lodges, with gravel to trailheads.
For rock art and Sani Pass.

bestTime.headline: March–May and September–November
bestTime.summary: The Drakensberg has hot, wet summers with thunderstorms and cold, dry winters, with snow on the peaks.

seasons.text: Warm and green, with afternoon thunderstorms.
Clear, warm days and cool nights.
Dry and sunny, but very cold at night, with snow.

bestTime.avoid: Summer afternoons for hiking, when storms and lightning are common.

days.afternoon: A short walk to a pool.

days.title: Rock art
days.morning: A guided walk to rock art.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you stay safe in the mountains.
tips: Check the weather. Storms and mist can arrive suddenly.
Register at park offices before hiking.
Bring layers, sun protection and waterproofs.
Take a guide for longer routes.
Start walks early to avoid afternoon storms.
Fill up with fuel and cash before arriving.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Drakensberg?
Is Tugela Falls really the second highest waterfall?
faq.a: It is often described so, at about 948 metres in five drops, though rankings vary by definition.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: March to May and September to November.

faq.q: Can I hike without a guide?
faq.a: Many day walks are fine without one. Take a guide for longer routes and rock art.
Nights are cold, even in summer, and winters can be freezing.
It is about 4 to 5 hours by road.
